newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA STOCKS CONSOLIDATE ON CRACKDOWN - PAPER. [CORRECTED 03:04 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CHINA STOCKS CONSOLIDATE ON CRACKDOWN - PAPER. [CORRECTED 03:04 GMT]

text.p: China's stock markets have consolidated in the past few weeks due to an official crackdown, which has helped to curb speculation and increased the supply of shares, the China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday.
"Share prices on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges have not risen in the past few weeks as investors had expected but have instead consolidated," the newspaper said in a commentary.
"All sorts of (measures) have put great pressure on the stock indices;" (corrects the quotation from "An official crackdown has contributed to the consolidation") it said.
Beijing had allowed the issue of large amounts of new shares in the past few months with a one-day record of 480 million new shares listed on China's two bourses on June 26 alone, the newspaper said.
"New share issues have exerted heavy pressure on the stock indices and prevented them from rising," it said.
In addition, Beijing has banned state banks, state enterprises and listed firms from trading on the stock markets, effectively cutting fund supply, it said.

The newspaper said the crackdown had served to curb excessive speculation, but the recent weak performance of the stock markets indicated a need to foster institutional investors to stabilise share prices.
Shanghai-based brokers said trading on China's seven-year-old stock markets was dominated by retail investors, whose numbers are currently estimated at around 30 million.
Due to a lack of investment funds and institutional market makers, share prices have fluctuated sharply, causing instability in the market, they said.
